source_context.text: Training compares the model's predicted token probabilities with the next tokens in the training examples. A learning rate that is too large can make training unstable, whereas a very small learning rate can slow improvement. Overfitting occurs when improved training performance fails to translate into performance on unseen examples. Dropout is a regularization technique that randomly disables some activations during training; ordinary inference uses the trained network without that random disabling. Early stopping uses validation performance to decide when to end training, rather than selecting a stopping point using the held-out test results.

describes.definition: SOURCE gives an account of the complete subject or phenomenon TARGET, without asserting causation, subtype or parthood.

stores.definition: SOURCE holds, retains, or performs storage of TARGET. TARGET is the stored content, not its destination. Explicit occurrence qualifiers specify storage format, medium or conditions.

is_a.definition: SOURCE is a subtype or kind of TARGET, not a component or instance.

causes.definition: SOURCE causally produces the explicit event TARGET, not merely permitting it. TARGET names the action or change, not its affected object.

source_context.text: The tutor's language model uses a decoder-only transformer to process text. A tokenizer divides an input passage into tokens, and an embedding layer maps those tokens to numerical vectors. Positional information helps the transformer distinguish sequences containing the same tokens in different orders. In each attention layer, self-attention combines information from token representations. A causal attention mask prevents a position from attending to later positions when the model predicts the next token. This restriction applies during both training and generation. Attention can connect information across a passage, but the model's finite context window limits the amount of text available in a single request. An attention weight does not establish that the associated claim is true.

It explains the internal workings of decoder-only transformers, including tokenization, causal attention masks, and the distinction between attention weights and factual truth. The text covers optimization techniques such as backpropagation, learning rate management, and regularization methods like dropout and early stopping to mitigate overfitting. Post-training strategies are addressed through weight quantization for memory efficiency and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for context augmentation, alongside the evaluation of retrieval quality versus answer generation accuracy, specifically focusing on factual correctness, uncertainty handling, and identifying disagreements between source passages.

source_context.text: The tutor's language model uses a decoder-only transformer to process text. A tokenizer divides an input passage into tokens, and an embedding layer maps those tokens to numerical vectors. Positional information helps the transformer distinguish sequences containing the same tokens in different orders. In each attention layer, self-attention combines information from token representations. A causal attention mask prevents a position from attending to later positions when the model predicts the next token. This restriction applies during both training and generation. Attention can connect information across a passage, but the model's finite context window limits the amount of text available in a single request. An attention weight does not establish that the associated claim is true.

source_context.text: Training compares the model's predicted token probabilities with the next tokens in the training examples. A loss function measures prediction error, and backpropagation computes gradients used by an optimizer to update model parameters. The learning rate controls the size of those updates. A learning rate that is too large can make training unstable, whereas a very small learning rate can slow improvement. Overfitting occurs when improved training performance fails to translate into performance on unseen examples. Dropout is a regularization technique that randomly disables some activations during training; ordinary inference uses the trained network without that random disabling. Early stopping uses validation performance to decide when to end training, rather than selecting a stopping point using the held-out test results.

source_context.text: After training, the tutor uses quantization and retrieval-augmented generation for different purposes. Weight quantization stores model parameters with fewer bits, reducing the memory required to store those parameters, although an aggressive reduction in precision can degrade answer quality. Retrieval-augmented generation supplies relevant course passages when the tutor answers a question. A retrieval encoder maps the question and document passages into embeddings, and a similarity search selects candidate passages from an index. The selected passages are added to the language model's context. Updating this document index can make revised course material available without retraining the language model. Retrieval does not itself change the model's parameters, and a highly ranked passage can still be irrelevant, outdated, or incorrect.
